title: Mixed-cup CoefficientData
statement:
With the global setting and stages of [def-sf-mixed-cup-coefficient-passages], take at every finite subextension and every positive finite level the existing normalized six-functor construction datum of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product]. For a separated finite-type geometric space and a compactification of its structure map, define its compact and ordinary coefficient-cohomology functors at each stage by the recorded support or direct operation followed by its point fibre [sk-def-ops]. Define its cup arrow to be the corresponding recorded finite, integral, rational or common-stage mixed cup. At field stages apply the prescribed carrier lift and its tensorator [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-rational-compatibility]. Define source and target coordinate isomorphisms and hence the same cup in tensor-of-cohomology coordinates.

The scalar functors preserve the finite-Tor constructible domains [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and the recorded tensors [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] preserve those domains; define their restrictions using these membership assertions. The point tensorator is that of the universal ordinary derived coefficient extension, and its identity and composition normalizations are the ordinary balancing and reassociation maps on every flat-term K-flat representative [def-sf-mixed-cup-normalized-scalars]. Define a site tensor comparison to be an isomorphism between scalar extension of the recorded tensor input and the tensor of the two extended inputs. Equal actual coefficient-ring maps have their literal equality-induced point-functor identification. All functors and cup arrows in these definitions are the existing constructions. The recorded construction data used here is that of [def-sf-operation-stages].

source.place: Final coefficient compatibility sentence; item proof steps 2–9: canonical comparison normalizations.

proof.text: For the finite scalar generator of change_domain, transport the input along the counit of sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence to the fixed-ModuleCat presentation. Apply closedScalarDomains_scalar of [lem-coef-closed-scalar-domains] to its existing Tor interval. The canonical realizationScalarIso of [lem-finite-compact-support-scalar-transport] identifies the fixed-scalar result with the actual pbcDerivedExtend of the input. Transport bounded constructibility using [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated]; transport Tor amplitude by composing each test-representative isomorphism with this isomorphism. Both input and output quotient levels are positive, and X is separated and finite type by its SixFunctorSpace property.

For integral reduction, use bounded constructibility of every reduction from the integral ambient object property and its uniform Tor interval from the domain property. For integral extension, the actual siteChange output already belongs to sfIntegralConstructibleCategory. The coefficient prime is a unit in D.k by finiteFieldDatumPrimeUnit of [lem-weil-structure-direct-images-constructible]; map this unit to every residue field of X. The equality of predicates in [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives the integral finite-Tor condition for that output.

The rational, localization and closure generators land in the full domain by definition. Identity preservation is the input property. For a composite, apply the induction hypothesis for its first passage to form an object of the intermediate full subcategory, then the induction hypothesis for its second passage. This proves change_domain for all passage expressions and defines the stated restricted functor without any changed object or morphism maps.

For tensor_domain, split on the coefficient stage. The finite tensor functor supplied by the recorded operation datum already has the finite-Tor full subcategory as its codomain, so take its object property. The integral tensor output is an object of sfIntegralConstructibleCategory; use the same residue-prime units and [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] as in Step 2. The two field domains are top. All remaining constructions are the existing stagewise cup and cohomology arrows and their stated coordinate isomorphisms.
